sections.category: Alibaba makes Qwen3.8-Max generally available at 2.4 trillion parameters and promises the open weights next week

bullets.body: Alibaba took Qwen3.8-Max generally available today, the largest model the Qwen family has shipped: 2.4 trillion total parameters with roughly 95 billion active per token, a sparse mixture-of-experts layout paired with a hybrid attention scheme meant to hold latency and compute below what a dense model of that size would demand. The model page lists a million-token context window, though maximum input is 991,000 tokens and 983,000 with thinking enabled, and it accepts text, images and video and returns text. Arena's leaderboards place it second on Vision Arena and fourth on Frontend Code Arena, and Alibaba pitches it on autonomous coding and long-horizon agent work. API pricing is two dollars per million input tokens and six dollars per million output. The part that matters for anyone running models on their own hardware is the follow-on rather than the flagship: Alibaba says it will open the weights next week and add a smaller Qwen3.8-27B alongside them, which would put a frontier-scale Chinese model and a workstation-scale sibling into the same release window.

sections.category: Microsoft's Project Perception reaches its public-preview date inside Defender, with red, blue and green agent teams handing work to each other

bullets.body: The preview date Microsoft set a week ago when it introduced Project Perception arrived today, and the system is now open to the public inside Microsoft Defender. Perception coordinates three sets of agents: red team agents that map paths to compromise before an attacker walks them, blue team agents that investigate and decide what constitutes meaningful risk, and green team agents that take corrective action and harden defences. Microsoft's own description has them handing off to each other automatically rather than parking in a queue for a human between stages. Underneath sits MAI-Cyber-1-Flash, the company's first in-house model built specifically for security work; Microsoft reports its MDASH vulnerability-finding product with that model scoring 96 percent on the CyberGym benchmark, twelve points above Anthropic's Claude Mythos, at close to half the cost of the MDASH configuration Microsoft sells today. Perception is priced as a consumption-based service, which is the question a preview exists to answer: whether the bill stays legible once teams run these loops continuously rather than in demos. Autonomous remediation is deliberately staged, starting with reversible actions such as isolating a machine.

sections.category: Horizon3 raises 250 million dollars at more than a two-billion valuation for autonomous penetration testing

bullets.body: Horizon3 announced a 250 million dollar Series E today at a valuation above two billion dollars, roughly triple the 650 million dollar valuation it carried out of its Series D in June 2025. NightDragon and NEA, both already shareholders, co-led. The round was oversubscribed and drew seven new investors — Acrew Capital, Blue Cloud Ventures, Demeter Group, Singapore's EDBI, PSG, SAIC and Sapphire Ventures — alongside five returning backers including Qualcomm Ventures and Craft Ventures. NightDragon founder Dave DeWalt, previously chief executive of both FireEye and McAfee, joins the board together with managing director Morgan Kyauk. The company sells an autonomous penetration-testing platform and is pushing from finding weaknesses into remediating them without a human in the loop; it says it approached 100 million dollars in annual recurring revenue last year, growing 120 percent year over year. The pitch it chose for the raise is that offence and defence are now both automated and racing each other — and that framing is what the round prices.

sections.category: A founder says coding agents rebuilt a CUDA-equivalent stack for someone else's accelerator in about ten hours

bullets.body: Jeremy Nixon, who left Google Brain to found Infinity last year, says his team pointed AI coding agents at d-Matrix silicon and had CUDA-equivalent software running in roughly ten hours, reaching about 92 percent of the Corsair part's theoretical peak on tensor-parallel matrix multiplication across all thirty-two of its compute units. Within ten days, he says, three frontier models were running end to end on the chip with every layer written from scratch. The agent doing the writing is called Ignition; it generates, tests and tunes the compute kernels that decide how efficiently a given accelerator runs a model — historically the work that costs a challenger vendor a specialist team and several years, and the reason porting rarely happens. Two supporting arguments arrived with the claim: Rebellions' Marshall Choy says CUDA "is no longer a factor" for inference, and Modular's Chris Lattner likens running AI on CUDA's graphics-inherited stack to squeezing a desktop operating system onto a phone. Against them, Futurum's Daniel Newman points at Nvidia's December purchase of SchedMD, which maintains the Slurm scheduler, and argues the moat got deeper rather than shallower. Infinity closed a 15 million dollar seed at a 100 million valuation last month with OpenAI and Anthropic researchers among the backers, so the claim is early and self-interested — but it is the first version of this argument that comes with a named partner chip and a stopwatch.

sections.category: Unsloth ships 2026.8.2 the day after 2026.8.1, and the change is about getting weights downloaded rather than trained

bullets.body: Unsloth published 2026.8.2 to PyPI today, one release after 2026.8.1, with unsloth-zoo moving to the matching version the same day. The substance is not a kernel or a new model family: downloads now fall back automatically from XET to plain HTTP when XET stalls, and memory use during a transfer is much reduced. The team frames it as stability — making a large weight pull finish instead of hanging — which reads as a direct answer to the fetch problems trailing the recent DeepSeek-V4 0731 and Kimi K3 support work rather than as a new capability. The remainder is interface alignment and chat-window fixes. Worth noting for anyone tracking the project by its repository rather than by its package index: the only commits on the main branch today were a merge and a changelog edit, and the release notes for this increment were appended as an August 3 section to the existing beta tag from late July instead of being cut as a fresh one, so PyPI and the changelog are where the version bump is actually visible.

sections.category: Bay Area / SV AI meet-up events

bullets.body: Las Vegas is the centre of gravity this week. Black Hat USA 2026 is mid-stride at Mandalay Bay: trainings run Saturday, August 1 through tomorrow, Tuesday, August 4; six summits land on Tuesday, August 4, one of them the one-day AI Summit; briefings and the Business Hall follow on Wednesday, August 5 and Thursday, August 6, with recordings available on demand for thirty days from August 14. Ai4 opens its pre-conference programme at The Venetian today, Monday, August 3 — technical and business summits, an applied AI research conference run with Colorado State, hands-on training courses with General Assembly, and industry meetups — before the main conference runs Tuesday, August 4 to Thursday, August 6, with roughly 12,000 attendees, 1,000 speakers and 400 exhibitors across close to a million square feet, headlined by Geoffrey Hinton, Fei-Fei Li and Andrew Ng. FMS: The Future of Memory and Storage marks its twentieth year at the Santa Clara Convention Center and the Hyatt Regency over the same three days, and is the place the memory squeeze gets discussed by the people causing it. DEF CON 34 then takes the LVCC West Hall from Thursday, August 6 to Sunday, August 9; late pre-registration at 600 dollars closed on Friday, July 31, and the door price is 520 dollars cash, so the door is now the cheaper way in. The badge is built on bunnie Huang's open-source Baochip and keeps working afterwards as a security token, password manager and hardware security module. AI Village takes Room W603 on Level 1 of the LVCC from August 6 with competitions, Creator Stage talks, poster presentations, fireside chats and demos, and runs HalCTF, the Hostile Autonomous Layer capture-the-flag: teams of up to five ship an agent as an OCI container capped at 2.5 GB, or use the reference agent, against sandboxed targets; thirteen models from 2B to 120B parameters are hosted centrally so the entry cost is code rather than GPUs, scoring decays as challenges fall with first-blood solutions worth the most, bonuses go to teams that win with smaller models, and first place takes a DGX Spark.

bullets.body: Closest to home on the security track, SecurityWeek's AI Risk Summit is at the Ritz-Carlton in Half Moon Bay on Tuesday, August 11 and Wednesday, August 12. The full pass is 1,895 dollars and steps to 2,195 after Friday, August 7; it covers the co-located CISO Forum Summer Summit, a welcome reception on Monday, August 10, a VIP dinner over the bay on the Tuesday, breakfast, lunch and dinner across both days, evening networking by the fire pits, post-conference materials and a discounted room rate subject to availability. The SecurityWeek Golf Classic on Thursday, August 13 at Half Moon Bay Golf Links is an optional, capacity-limited add-on. Two speaking deadlines matter this month for anyone who would rather present than pay: Zenity's AI Agent Security Summit takes talk submissions until Monday, August 17 for its London edition on Thursday, October 8, and until Friday, August 21 for New York on Wednesday, October 21. Submissions must be vendor-neutral and grounded in original research, live demos or real case studies rather than product pitches; selected speakers attend free with up to 800 dollars of airfare and two hotel nights covered, and may be routed to whichever city fits. The call-for-speakers page states there are two more summits in 2026 and lists no Asia edition, while Zenity's own events page continues to describe an Asia expansion with no city and no date — the same gap carried here for weeks, and a third-party report giving it a Tokyo date in September is still uncorroborated at source. The separately-run AI Security Summit holds its San Francisco edition on Thursday, October 15 across a leadership track for the people who own AI risk and a practitioner track for the people building and breaking the systems; its San Francisco page lists a London edition and a Paris call for talks as the other 2026 stops, neither dated, and the Nordics and Sydney editions carried here previously still do not appear on it. Colliding with that same Thursday, October 15 is the San Francisco AI Engineering and Infrastructure Summit, which despite the name sits at the Crowne Plaza Palo Alto on El Camino Real, 8:30 AM to 3:30 PM, free to attend, closed-door and practitioner-led with its speakers already set rather than an open call. Further out: SANS runs its AI Cybersecurity Summit on Monday, November 2 and Tuesday, November 3 at the Hilton Arlington Rosslyn, hybrid, at 525 dollars for the summit alone, with a 229 dollar room block closing October 9 and a refund cutoff of October 14; OWASP Global AppSec USA takes the Hyatt Regency San Francisco on Thursday, November 5 and Friday, November 6 with hands-on training from November 2 to 4; and the 19th ACM Workshop on Artificial Intelligence and Security meets Sunday, November 15 in The Hague alongside the 33rd ACM Conference on Computer and Communications Security, its paper deadline having closed on July 24, with reviews due September 7, notifications September 9 and camera-ready September 16.

bullets.body: On the silicon calendar, Hot Chips 2026 runs Sunday, August 23 to Tuesday, August 25 at Memorial Auditorium at Stanford in Palo Alto and is hybrid. The early rate has lapsed, so anyone booking now pays standard; late registration stays open through the conference itself, though in-person capacity can sell out, and refunds can be requested until 11:59 PM PDT on Wednesday, August 19 less a 25 dollar processing fee. The virtual pass carries videos, presentation PDFs and Slack channels for both the tutorial and the conference days. Sunday, August 23 is the tutorial day: a memory tutorial in the morning covering HBM base die and advanced packaging, 3D DRAM accelerators for generative inference and high-bandwidth flash in AI compute systems, then a RISC-V tutorial in the afternoon on profiles and platforms, enterprise open-source development, interoperability with NVIDIA GPUs and automotive use. The conference days are Monday, August 24 and Tuesday, August 25: two CPU sessions spanning IBM's Z and LinuxONE processor, Intel's Wildcat Lake Core Series 3 and Diamond Rapids Xeon, NVIDIA's Vera CPU, Fujitsu's MONAKA and an Arm server part for AI workloads; a Waymo keynote on autonomous driving plus an automotive session with BOS Semiconductors' Eagle-N and Waymo's sensor-fusion processor; and a GPU session with NVIDIA's Rubin, AMD's Instinct MI400 Series and Intel's Crescent Island. Tuesday adds an FPGA session in which AMD presents a secure computing SoC alongside Versal RF — worth a note for anyone tracking the security-silicon intersection — a memory session with Samsung's LPDDR5X processing-in-memory part and XCENA's MX1 CXL device, a networking session with Broadcom's Thor Ultra, NVIDIA's BlueField-4 and Spectrum-X and Mojo Vision's optical I/O, and two accelerator sessions covering Meta's MTIA, an NVIDIA LPU accelerator, Cerebras' Wafer Scale Engine, Microsoft's MAIA 200, SambaNova's SN50 RDU, Google's TPU family and OpenAI on its chip development. After that the infrastructure calendar runs: the AI Infra Summit at the Santa Clara Convention Center from Tuesday, September 15 to Thursday, September 17 with roughly 316 sessions across a main stage plus data-and-models, compute, data-movement, AI-data-centre and physical-AI tracks, two expo theatres and workshops; the Edge AI and Vision Innovation Forum in San Jose on Wednesday, September 16; the OCP Global Summit in San Jose from Monday, October 12 to Thursday, October 15; NVIDIA's GTC Berlin from Tuesday, October 20 to Thursday, October 22, with GTC not returning to San Jose until March 2027; and SC26 in Chicago from Sunday, November 15 to Friday, November 20.

bullets.body: Ray Summit is at the San Francisco Marriott Marquis from Monday, August 24 to Wednesday, August 26 — a training day on the Monday, then two days of keynotes and breakouts — at 400 dollars for the summit and 450 dollars with training, with a five-pass bundle listed at 750 dollars for all five against a 2,250 dollar list price. The training day covers multimodal data pipelines, distributed foundation-model training, production inference with Ray Serve, physical AI and robotics, real-time search and recommendation, and post-training and serving. The first vLLM Conference is co-located, hosted by Inferact, and included in every Ray Summit pass, with more than twenty speakers across vLLM infrastructure, hardware backends, production deployment patterns and ecosystem integrations, including vLLM creator and core maintainer Woosuk Kwon, now Inferact's chief technology officer, and core maintainer Simon Mo, now its chief executive, plus contributors from NVIDIA, AMD, Google TPU, Intel, Meta and PyTorch, Hugging Face and Red Hat. Ray Summit's own keynotes come from Anyscale co-founders Robert Nishihara and Ion Stoica, NVIDIA's Bryan Catanzaro, Torc's Felix Heide, Lila Sciences' Andrew Beam and, newly listed, Bedrock's Vincent Gonguet. The ACM AI Leadership Summit is in Atlanta from Sunday, August 30 to Wednesday, September 2. Four San Francisco events still collide at the end of September: CoreWeave's Fully Connected at Moscone South from Tuesday, September 29 to Thursday, October 1, its early-bird rate lapsed so the standard pass is 1,299 dollars against 899 before, with three tracks covering AI infrastructure, model advances, and agent evaluation and monitoring, and a keynote roster running to CoreWeave chief executive Mike Intrator and chief technology officer Peter Salanki, NVIDIA's Ian Buck, Fei-Fei Li of Stanford and World Labs, Sarah Guo of Conviction and Liquid AI chief operating officer Jeffrey Li; The AI Conference at Pier 48 Sheds A and B over the same window with five tracks, more than 5,500 attendees and more than 120 speakers, its September 29 workshops and Hack Day capped at 350 and sold out, with two-day pass holders promised first notice if inventory reopens; OpenAI's DevDay at Fort Mason on Tuesday, September 29 with applications already closed; and Newcomer's Machine Earning AI Summit in San Francisco the same day with applications open. After that: the Runway AI Summit on Wednesday, September 30; World Summit AI in Amsterdam on Wednesday, October 7 and Thursday, October 8; the PyTorch Conference in San Jose on Tuesday, October 20 and Wednesday, October 21; AGNTCon and MCPCon North America on Thursday, October 22 and Friday, October 23 at the San Jose McEnery Convention Center under the Linux Foundation, built around the Model Context Protocol, agent infrastructure and the security and observability of production agent systems, with the call for proposals closed since June 7 so what is left is attendance; GitHub Universe at Fort Mason on Wednesday, October 28 and Thursday, October 29; the application-only AI Engineer Code Summit in San Francisco from Wednesday, November 11 to Friday, November 13 with speaker submissions closing October 11; Newcomer's Cerebral Valley AI Summit in San Francisco on Thursday, November 12; AWS re:Invent from Monday, November 30 to Friday, December 4; NeurIPS in December; and The AI Summit New York on Wednesday, December 9 and Thursday, December 10.

bullets.body: On the robotics calendar, the last open submission window for IEEE-RAS Humanoids 2026 closes today: workshop, tutorial and competition team proposals are due Monday, August 3 anywhere on Earth, with the paper deadline having closed July 27 and the supplementary-video window July 30. Competition decisions follow on September 21, workshop and tutorial decisions on September 28, paper acceptance notifications on October 6, early-bird registration on October 16 and camera-ready papers on October 26, with the conference itself at the Santa Clara Convention Center from Sunday, December 6 to Wednesday, December 9 — public forums on the 6th, workshops and tutorials on the 7th, and paper sessions on the 8th and 9th. On AI Tinkerers, Columbus runs today, Monday, August 3, 5:30 to 8 PM EDT. Then Paris with Paris.rb, 7 to 10 PM CEST, and a Seattle AI dev-tools track, 6 to 9 PM PDT, both tomorrow, Tuesday, August 4; Singapore with Redis, 6 to 9 PM local, and a Seattle founders' dinner on trust and long-running agents, 6 to 9 PM PDT, on Wednesday, August 5; the Los Angeles builder meetup and live demos on Thursday, August 6, 6 to 8 PM PDT; a Medellín voice-agents challenge with 1,000 dollars in prizes and the New York Vision Hack on live feeds and open data, 4 to 10 PM EDT, both on Friday, August 7; then the Mombasa chapter launch, 9 AM to noon EAT, and a Dubai demo day, 11:30 AM to 3 PM local, on Saturday, August 8. A five-city Tuesday follows on August 11 — a Valencia go-to-market teardown, an Upstate New York build night, Chicago with Cloudflare and PostHog, Houston, and a Seattle AI-and-biology demo night with NVIDIA and the Allen Institute for AI — then three more on Wednesday, August 12 in Valencia, Brussels on the agentic software lifecycle, and Raleigh; then Bremen on Friday, August 14; and on Saturday, August 15 both the inaugural Da Nang meetup and a newly-listed Islamabad and Rawalpindi session, 2 to 5 PM PKT. Newly on the calendar further out: Orange County on Wednesday, August 19, Boston on Thursday, September 3 and Columbus again on Monday, September 7. Nothing is dated in San Francisco, San Jose or Pleasanton. The Palo Alto meetup carried here for Tuesday, August 18 still cannot be confirmed — that chapter page refused the request again today, and the date does not appear on the global calendar either, so treat it as unverified rather than scheduled.
